conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: I feel pretty low today. I was in a crowded place earlier, and I couldn’t shake this feeling like I was back in that moment. Just a bunch of faces around, and my heart started racing. It really knocked the wind out of me, you know?

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That sounds difficult. When you were in that crowded place, did you notice any specific thoughts or images that came to mind as your heart started racing?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Honestly, it all just went blank for a second, but then I could almost see flashes of my past. I just felt this overwhelming urge to get out, like I was trapped there. It’s like I couldn’t remember why I was even there in the first place, but all I wanted was to escape.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: It sounds intense to experience that feeling of being trapped. In that moment when you wanted to escape, did you have any thoughts about how to make that situation feel safer or more manageable?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Not really. I just wanted to get out as fast as I could. It felt like my mind went into survival mode, and I wasn't thinking straight. I couldn’t even focus on what might help; I just needed air, like the walls were closing in.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That sounds really stressful. Once you were able to get out, how did your feelings or thoughts shift afterward?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: When I finally got outside, I felt a bit of relief wash over me, but it didn’t last long. I stood there, breathing heavily, and all I could think about was how I didn’t want to go back inside anywhere. It’s like the relief turned into this nagging reminder of how vulnerable I felt in there.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: It makes sense that the relief would be short-lived after such a strong experience. After that moment outside, did any specific thoughts or concerns come to mind about being in similar situations in the future?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Yeah, I started worrying a lot about the next time I’d have to be in a crowded place. It’s like I can't shake this dread that it’ll happen again, and I’ll lose control. I could see myself making excuses to avoid situations just to keep that feeling at bay, and it sucks.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That sounds challenging to deal with. In the moments since that experience, have you noticed any physical sensations or emotions that come up when you think about being in crowded places again?
